messages:
alex: Quick sync — I'm about to merge the change that makes the client send an \"x-accept-model\" header by default. Two quick questions: 1) does the server still need to treat missing header as 'latest-unpinned' for the next 30 days? 2) can we add a short deprecation window note in the response when we fallback?

rachel: yes to (1) — we keep missing header semantics for 30 days to give SDKs time. For (2) I'm +1 but prefer a terse response flag rather than a full message body change. Something like `X-Compat-Note: model-fallback=v1 -> v0.9 (deprecate 2026-05-15)`

dan: fwiw, adding a header seems safer than changing JSON shape. Clients ignore unknown headers. If we do the header, can we also add a `debug_id` in the response so customers can correlate fallbacks?

kevin: agree with dan. Implementation note: runtime will pick fallback model variants automatically; we can emit `X-Fallback-Model` with the id. Keep the deprecation date in the header too.

alex: sounds good. I'll update the PR with `X-Compat-Note` and `X-Fallback-Model`. Quick code snippet I plan to add to the handler:```http
// pseudocode
if (!req.headers['x-accept-model']) {
  res.setHeader('X-Compat-Note', 'accept-model-missing;expires=2026-05-15');
  selected = runtime.selectDefaultModel();
  res.setHeader('X-Fallback-Model', selected.id);
}
```

rachel: nit: use ISO date `2026-05-15T00:00:00Z` in header value to avoid ambiguity. Also please spell out version semantics in the header value e.g. `accept-model-missing;expiry=2026-05-15T00:00:00Z;policy=latest-unpinned`

alex: good call. I'll update. Also pinging @dan for review on the response header naming and @kevin for runtime sanity checks.

deploy-bot: CI passed for branch `feature/accept-header-default` — deployment queued to staging. :rocket:

dan: quick question — any clients that rely on implicit default selection behavior (e.g., mobile SDK older than v1.2)? If so, we should put a note in the SDK changelog and add a feature-flag to avoid surprise.

kevin: mobile SDKs older than v1.2 are <1% of traffic but still active. Proposal: do a canary rollout of the header-enforced behavior behind a config flag per-customer for 2 weeks, then flip global. Add telemetry tag `compat_header_rollout` so we can measure 4xx/5xx changes.

alex: action items I can own: 1) update PR with header names + ISO expiry format, 2) add telemetry tag in runtime, 3) create a short blurb for SDK changelog and changelog PR (cc @rachel). I'll also add a small playbook line in the deprecation doc: how to revert if we see errors.

rachel: thanks. +1 on the canary plan. Can you create the canary config and schedule it for next Tue?

alex: will do, targeting Tue 09:00 PT. I'll post another update here once the staging rollout finishes.

kevin: if you need a quick hand on the canary config I can pair Tuesday morning.

alex: thanks all. tagging this resolved for now unless someone objects. :white_check_mark:
